He, exalted is He, censures those who turn away from obedience to Allah: ﴿So he did not believe [in the Message] nor did he pray. But he denied and turned away﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 31-32]. ﴿And gave a little and then stopped﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he obeyed a little, then cut it off. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others. 'Ikrimah and Sa'id said: it is like a people digging a well, who find a rock in the midst of the digging that prevents them from completing the work, so they say, "We have stopped [akda-na]," and abandon the work.

* *

His saying: ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ That is: does this one, who has withheld his hand out of fear of spending and cut off his good deeds, have knowledge of the unseen, that what is in his hand will run out, so that he has withheld his kindness, and sees that clearly? That is: the matter is not so. Rather, he withheld from charity, kindness, righteousness and maintaining ties out of stinginess, avarice and anxiety. For this reason it has come in a hadith: "Spend, Bilal, and do not fear from the Lord of the Throne poverty" [Note: this comes from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Bilal and Ibn Mas'ud. As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: it was narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (2/280) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/341) through two routes from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from him. As for the hadith of Bilal: it was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/359) through the route of Abu Ishaq from Masruq, from him. As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: it was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/191) through the route of Yahya ibn Wathhab from Masruq, from him.] And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾ [Saba': 39].

* *

His saying: ﴿Has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa, and Ibrahim who fulfilled [his trust]?﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Thawri said: that is, he conveyed all that he was commanded.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ means he conveyed [the message] for Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ what he was commanded. Qatadah said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ the obedience of Allah, and delivered His message to His creation. This view is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it encompasses the one before it, and it is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. He carried out all the commands, abandoned all the prohibitions, and conveyed the message in full and complete form, and by this he merited being a leader for mankind, to be followed in all his states, actions and sayings. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 123].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-'Asqalani narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, and said: "Do you know what 'fulfilled' means?" I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: "He fulfilled the work of his day with four rak'ahs from the beginning of the day."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, and it is weak [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/43)].

Al-Tirmidhi said in his Jami': Abu Ja'far al-Samnani narrated to us, Abu Musbir narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd [in M and A: "Yahya ibn Sa'id"], from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu al-Darda' and Abu Dharr, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "Son of Adam, bow to Me in four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you at its end" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (475), and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: my father narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Zabban ibn Qa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Shall I not inform you why Allah named Ibrahim His friend, 'who fulfilled'? He used to say whenever he woke in the morning and in the evening: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17], until the end of the verse." Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, from [in M: "ibn"] Zabban, with it [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/43). al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (20/192) through both routes, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/117): "In it are weak narrators who were deemed trustworthy."

I say: in the first, there is Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak.

In the second, Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who is weak.

And in both, Zayyan ibn Fa'id, who is weak.]

Then He, exalted is He, began to explain what He had revealed in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa, so He said: ﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. That is: every soul that wronged itself by disbelief or some sin, the burden is upon it alone, and no one bears it for it, as He said: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to carry its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir: 18]. ﴿And that man will have only what he strives for﴾. That is: just as the burden of another is not placed upon him, similarly he does not obtain reward except what he himself has earned. From this noble verse, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who follow him, derived that the recitation of the Qur'an does not reach the dead by way of gifting its reward to them, because it is not of their work nor their earning. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recommend it to his community, nor urge them toward it, nor guide them to it, by explicit text or allusion, and nothing of this was transmitted from any of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. Had it been good, they would have preceded us to it. The domain of acts of worship is restricted to the texts and is not to be handled by various kinds of analogical reasoning (qiyas) and opinions. As for supplication and charity, these are agreed upon as reaching the dead, and are stated explicitly by the Lawgiver.

As for the hadith which Muslim narrated in his Sahih (authentic collection), from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, or ongoing charity after him, or knowledge from which benefit is gained" [Sahih Muslim no. (1631)]. These three are in reality from his striving, his effort and his work, as has come in the hadith: "The best of what a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings" [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/31), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (3528), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (1358), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (7/240), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]. Ongoing charity such as a waqf (endowment) and the like is among the traces of his work and endowment. Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12]. And the knowledge which he spread among the people, so that people followed it after him, is also from his striving and work. And it is established in the Sahih: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards."

* *

That is: He will inform you of it, and recompense you for it with the most complete recompense: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. Likewise He said here: ﴿Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense﴾. That is: the most abundant.

Al-Tirmidhi said in his Jami': Abu Ja'far al-Samnani narrated to us, Abu Musbir narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd [in M and A: "Yahya ibn Sa'id"], from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu al-Darda' and Abu Dharr, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "Son of Adam, bow to Me in four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you at its end" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (475), and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: my father narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Zabban ibn Qa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Shall I not inform you why Allah named Ibrahim His friend, 'who fulfilled'? In the second, Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who is weak.

And in both, Zayyan ibn Fa'id, who is weak.]

Then He, exalted is He, began to explain what He had revealed in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa, so He said: ﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. That is: every soul that wronged itself by disbelief or some sin, the burden is upon it alone, and no one bears it for it, as He said: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to carry its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir: 18]. ﴿And that man will have only what he strives for﴾. (1631)]. These three are in reality from his striving, his effort and his work, as has come in the hadith: "The best of what a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings" [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/31), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (3528), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (1358), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (7/240), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]. Ongoing charity such as a waqf (endowment) and the like is among the traces of his work and endowment. Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12]. And the knowledge which he spread among the people, so that people followed it after him, is also from his striving and work. And it is established in the Sahih: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards."

* *

His saying: ﴿And that his striving will be seen﴾. That is: on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And say: Work, and Allah will see your work, and His Messenger and the believers, and you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [al-Tawbah: 105]. That is: He will inform you of it, and recompense you for it with the most complete recompense: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. Likewise He said here: ﴿Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense﴾. That is: the most abundant.

He, exalted is He, censures those who turn away from obedience to Allah: ﴿So he did not believe [in the Message] nor did he pray. But he denied and turned away﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 31-32]. ﴿And gave a little and then stopped﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he obeyed a little, then cut it off. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others. 'Ikrimah and Sa'id said: it is like a people digging a well, who find a rock in the midst of the digging that prevents them from completing the work, so they say, "We have stopped [akda-na]," and abandon the work.

* *

His saying: ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ That is: does this one, who has withheld his hand out of fear of spending and cut off his good deeds, have knowledge of the unseen, that what is in his hand will run out, so that he has withheld his kindness, and sees that clearly? That is: the matter is not so. Rather, he withheld from charity, kindness, righteousness and maintaining ties out of stinginess, avarice and anxiety. For this reason it has come in a hadith: "Spend, Bilal, and do not fear from the Lord of the Throne poverty" [Note: this comes from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Bilal and Ibn Mas'ud. As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: it was narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (2/280) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/341) through two routes from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from him. As for the hadith of Bilal: it was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/359) through the route of Abu Ishaq from Masruq, from him. As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: it was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/191) through the route of Yahya ibn Wathhab from Masruq, from him.] And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾ [Saba': 39].

* *

His saying: ﴿Has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa, and Ibrahim who fulfilled [his trust]?﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Thawri said: that is, he conveyed all that he was commanded.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ means he conveyed [the message] for Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ what he was commanded. Qatadah said: ﴿fulfilled﴾ the obedience of Allah, and delivered His message to His creation. This view is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it encompasses the one before it, and it is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. He carried out all the commands, abandoned all the prohibitions, and conveyed the message in full and complete form, and by this he merited being a leader for mankind, to be followed in all his states, actions and sayings. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 123].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-'Asqalani narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, and said: "Do you know what 'fulfilled' means?" I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: "He fulfilled the work of his day with four rak'ahs from the beginning of the day."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, and it is weak [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/43)].

I say: in the first, there is Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak.

In the second, Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who is weak.

And in both, Zayyan ibn Fa'id, who is weak.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And that his striving will be seen﴾. That is: on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And say: Work, and Allah will see your work, and His Messenger and the believers, and you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [al-Tawbah: 105]. That is: He will inform you of it, and recompense you for it with the most complete recompense: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. Likewise He said here: ﴿Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense﴾. That is: the most abundant.

Allah the Exalted says, reporting: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final return﴾, meaning the return on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal stood among us and said: "O Banu Awd, I am the Messenger of Allah to you. You know that the return is to Allah, to Paradise or to the Fire."

Al-Baghawi mentioned, from the narration of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿And that to your Lord is the final return﴾, that he said: "There is no contemplation (of the Lord)."[1]

Al-Baghawi said: This is like what is reported from Abu Hurayrah as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith: "Contemplate the creation, and do not contemplate the Creator, for thought cannot encompass Him."

He cited it thus, but it is not preserved with this wording. What is in the Sahih is: "Satan comes to one of you and says: Who created such-and-such? Who created such-and-such? Until he says: Who created your Lord? When one of you reaches that, let him seek refuge in Allah and desist."[2]

In another hadith in the Sunan: "Contemplate the creatures of Allah, and do not contemplate the Essence of Allah, for Allah created an angel the distance between the lobe of whose ear and his shoulder is a journey of three hundred years," or as he said.[3]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, meaning: He created laughter and weeping in His servants, and caused them, though they are different from each other.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾, like His saying: ﴿He who created death and life﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2]. ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female, from a drop when it is emitted﴾, like His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected? Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned, and made of him two sexes, male and female. Is not that One able to give life to the dead?﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 36–40].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And that it is He who originates the second creation﴾, meaning: just as He created the first beginning, He is able to restore it, and this is the later creation on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And that it is He who enriches and grants possessions﴾, meaning: He gave His servants wealth and made it for them a lasting property with them, which they do not need to sell. This is the completion of His blessing upon them. On this interpretation revolves the speech of many of the commentators, among them Abu Salih, Ibn Jarir, and others. From Mujahid: ﴿aghna﴾ means "made wealthy" (mawwala), and ﴿aqna﴾ means "made to serve" (akhdam). Qatadah also said likewise.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also said: ﴿aghna﴾ means "gave," and ﴿aqna﴾ means "was pleased" (radda).

It was also said: its meaning is that He enriched Himself and made the creatures most in need of Him, as related by al-Hadrami ibn Lahiq.

It was also said: ﴿aghna﴾ means He enriches whomever He wills of His creation, and ﴿aqna﴾ means He makes whomever He wills of them poor, as stated by Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jarir related both, but they are far-fetched in terms of the wording.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others said: It is this blazing star which is called "Mirzam al-Jawza'" (the Orion's Tongue), which a group of the Arabs used to worship.

﴿And that He destroyed the former 'Ad﴾, and they are the people of Hud. They are also called 'Ad son of Iram son of Sam son of Nuh, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, of Iram, of the lofty pillars, the like of which was never created in the lands?﴾ [Al-Fajr: 6–8]. They were among the strongest, most powerful, and most insolent of people toward Allah and His Messenger, so Allah destroyed them ﴿with a violent screaming wind, which He subjected against them for seven nights and eight days in succession﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 6–7].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Thamud, and He spared none﴾, meaning: He destroyed them and left none of them alive. ﴿And the people of Nuh before,﴾ meaning: before these. ﴿Indeed, they were more wrongful and more transgressing﴾, meaning: more rebellious than those who came after them. ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾, meaning: the cities of Lot. He overturned them upon their people, making their highest part their lowest, and rained upon them stones of baked clay, layered and piled. Therefore He said: ﴿Then there covered them that which covered﴾, meaning: of the stones He sent upon them. ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those warned﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 173].

Qatadah said: In the cities of Lot there were four thousand thousand people [four million]. A valley of fire, pitch and tar, like the mouth of a furnace, blazed over them. Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his father, from Muhammad ibn Wahb ibn Atiyyah, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Khulayd, from him (Qatadah). It is very strange (gharib jiddan).

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you dispute?﴾, meaning: Concerning which of the blessings of Allah upon you, O human, will you be in doubt? Said by Qatadah.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you dispute?﴾ O Muhammad. The first (interpretation) is more appropriate, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

**﴿This is a warner of the warnings of old.﴾** Meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), **"of the warnings of old"**, that is, of their own kind. He was sent as they were sent, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say, I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9].

**﴿The Imminent Event has drawn near.﴾** That is, the near one has drawn close, and it is the Resurrection. **﴿None besides Allah can remove it.﴾** That is, no one other than Allah can then avert it, and none other than Him knows its knowledge.

Then Allah the Exalted said, rebuking the polytheists for their listening to the Qur'an, their turning away from it, and their distraction: **﴿Do you wonder﴾** at its being true? **﴿And laugh﴾** at it mockingly and derisively? **﴿And not weep﴾**, that is, as those who have certainty in it do, as He reported about them: ﴿They fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility﴾ [al-Isra: 109].

* *

As for His saying **﴿while you are sāmidūn﴾** (sāmidūn: the word is taken to mean those who are heedless, or who sing and stay up in merriment). Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Ghina" (singing). It is a Yemeni usage: *usmud lana* means "sing for us" (*ghanna lana*). Ikrimah also said the same.

In another narration from Ibn 'Abbas: *sāmidūn* means those who turn away (*mu'ridūn*). Mujahid and Ikrimah also said this. Al-Hasan said: heedless (*ghafilūn*). This is also a narration from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. In another narration from Ibn 'Abbas: those who are arrogant (*mustakbirūn*). Al-Suddi also held this view.

Then Allah said, commanding His servants to prostrate to Him, to worship Him by following His Messenger (ﷺ), and to affirm His oneness and sincerity: **﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him]﴾**, that is, humble yourselves before Him, be sincere to Him, and affirm His oneness.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) prostrated at [the recitation of] *al-Najm*, and the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn and the humans prostrated with him. He alone reported this, apart from Muslim.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us, Rabah narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ja'far ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Najm in Makkah, and he prostrated, and those with him prostrated. I raised my head and refused to prostrate. Al-Muttalib had not yet embraced Islam on that day. After that, he would not hear anyone recite it without prostrating with him.

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in *al-Salah*, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with the same chain.

**A hadith related to what preceded in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warnings of old. The Imminent Event has drawn near.﴾** The *nadhīr* (warner) is one who warns of evil that he witnesses and fears will befall those he warns, as He said: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾ [Saba': 46]. And in a hadith: "I am the naked warner" (*al-nadhīr al-'uryān*), meaning one whom the severity of the evil he witnessed hurried so that he did not take time to dress; rather, he hastened to warn his people before that. He came to them naked and in haste. This is consistent with His saying: ﴿The Imminent Event has drawn near﴾, that is, the near one has drawn close, meaning the Day of Resurrection, as He said at the beginning of the following surah: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. Imam Ahmad said:

Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to me, (I know of nothing except from Sahl ibn Sa'd), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Beware of trivial sins, for the example of trivial sins is like a people who camped in the bottom of a valley; one brought a stick, and another brought a stick, until they baked their bread. Indeed, trivial sins, if their doer is held accountable for them, will destroy him." Abu Hazim said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said — Abu Damrah said: I know of nothing except from Sahl ibn Sa'd — "My example and the example of the Hour is like these two," and he separated his middle finger from the one next to the thumb. Then he said: "My example and the example of the Hour is like two horses in a race," then he said: "My example and the example of the Hour is like a man whom his people sent as a scout; when he feared he would be overtaken, he waved his garment, [crying]: 'You have been reached! You have been reached!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am that [scout]."

It has supporting narrations from other routes, some *sahih* (authentic) and some *hasan* (good). And to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and in Him is trust and protection.

*End of the commentary on Surah al-Najm. To Allah belongs all praise and grace.*

I raised my head and refused to prostrate. Al-Muttalib had not yet embraced Islam on that day. After that, he would not hear anyone recite it without prostrating with him.

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in *al-Salah*, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with the same chain.

**A hadith related to what preceded in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warnings of old. The Imminent Event has drawn near.﴾** The *nadhīr* (warner) is one who warns of evil that he witnesses and fears will befall those he warns, as He said: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾ [Saba': 46]. And in a hadith: "I am the naked warner" (*al-nadhīr al-'uryān*), meaning one whom the severity of the evil he witnessed hurried so that he did not take time to dress; rather, he hastened to warn his people before that. He came to them naked and in haste. This is consistent with His saying: ﴿The Imminent Event has drawn near﴾, that is, the near one has drawn close, meaning the Day of Resurrection, as He said at the beginning of the following surah: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. Imam Ahmad said:

Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to me, (I know of nothing except from Sahl ibn Sa'd), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Beware of trivial sins, for the example of trivial sins is like a people who camped in the bottom of a valley; one brought a stick, and another brought a stick, until they baked their bread. Indeed, trivial sins, if their doer is held accountable for them, will destroy him." Abu Hazim said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said — Abu Damrah said: I know of nothing except from Sahl ibn Sa'd — "My example and the example of the Hour is like these two," and he separated his middle finger from the one next to the thumb. Then he said: "My example and the example of the Hour is like two horses in a race," then he said: "My example and the example of the Hour is like a man whom his people sent as a scout; when he feared he would be overtaken, he waved his garment, [crying]: 'You have been reached! You have been reached!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am that [scout]."

It has supporting narrations from other routes, some *sahih* (authentic) and some *hasan* (good). And to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and in Him is trust and protection.

*End of the commentary on Surah al-Najm. To Allah belongs all praise and grace.*
